atoms.name: mod
atoms.rule: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: neg
atoms.rule: - a is the negation of a.
atoms.plain: - a is the negation of a.

atoms.name: pitch_transpose
atoms.rule: a v1_u266F_ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u266F_ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_up
atoms.rule: a v1_u21C8_ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21C8_ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_down
atoms.rule: a v1_u21CA_ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21CA_ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_interval
atoms.rule: a v1_u27F7_ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.
atoms.plain: a v1_u27F7_ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.

atoms.name: pitch_invert
atoms.rule: a v1_u21C5_ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u21C5_ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_retrograde
atoms.rule: a v1_u27F2_ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.
atoms.plain: a v1_u27F2_ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.

atoms.name: pitch_scale_step
atoms.rule: a v1_u266C_ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u266C_ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_major_triad
atoms.rule: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_minor_triad
atoms.rule: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_repeat
atoms.rule: a v1_u2941_ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.
atoms.plain: a v1_u2941_ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_concat
atoms.rule: a v1_u22C8_ b plays melody a followed by melody b.
atoms.plain: a v1_u22C8_ b plays melody a followed by melody b.

atoms.name: pitch_melody_equal
atoms.rule: a v1_u224E_ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.
atoms.plain: a v1_u224E_ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.

atoms.name: pitch_note_equal
atoms.rule: a v1_u2250_ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.
atoms.plain: a v1_u2250_ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.

domain.en: A note is a MIDI number from 0 to 127; 60 is C4. A melody is a list of notes with durations in beats.
Integers give semitone steps, repeat counts and recursive counts.

settings.en: The key and scale used by the scale step v1_u266C_.
A recursive call repeats its step at most this many times; larger counts give NaN.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: f1
operators.plain: Append b to a, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: f2
operators.plain: If a equals [D4:1 F4:2], reverse the notes in a, then apply f12 to the result and [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2]; otherwise reverse the notes in a.

operators.name: f3
operators.definition: a f3 b = { a, if b == 0; (a f3 (b - 1)) f24, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a f3 (b + 1)) f24, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply f24 to the current value.

operators.name: f4
operators.plain: Apply f1 to a and b, then append [D4:1 F4:2] to it.

operators.name: f5
operators.plain: Transpose a by b semitones, then measure the semitones from it to C5.

operators.name: f6
operators.plain: Build a minor triad on a, then mirror it around C5.

operators.name: f7
operators.definition: a f7 b = { (a v1_u266F_ b) f6 }
operators.plain: Transpose a by b semitones, then apply f6 to the result.

operators.name: f8
operators.plain: Take the remainder when dividing 4 by the semitones from a to b.

operators.name: f9
operators.plain: Test whether D4 is the same note as a moved by b semitones.

operators.name: f10
operators.plain: Build a major triad on a, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: f11
operators.plain: Test whether [D4:1 F4:2] equals a mirrored around b.

operators.name: f12
operators.plain: Append a f1 b to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: f13
operators.plain: Apply f1 to [D4:1 F4:2] and (a f4 b).

operators.name: f14
operators.plain: Measure the semitones from a to b, then take the remainder when dividing it by 4.

operators.name: f15
operators.plain: Apply f7 to C5 and (a f5 b).

operators.name: f16
operators.plain: Apply f1 to a and b, then apply f4 to the result and [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: f17
operators.plain: Apply f10 to a, then mirror it around E4.

operators.name: f18
operators.plain: Apply f12 to [D4:1 F4:2] and (a followed by b).

operators.name: f19
operators.definition: a f19 b = { (a v1_u266F_ b) v1_u266C_, if a v1_u2250_ 60; a v1_u266F_ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, transpose a by b semitones, then move it up one step of C major; otherwise transpose a by b semitones.

operators.name: f20
operators.plain: If a is the same note as E4, apply f12 to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] and (a f7 b); otherwise compute a f7 b.

operators.name: f21
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply f1 to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] and (a f7 b); otherwise compute a f7 b.

operators.name: f22
operators.plain: If a equals [G4:1], mirror a around b, then apply f12 to the result and [D4:1 F4:2]; otherwise mirror a around b.

operators.name: f23
operators.definition: a f23 b = { (a f15 b) v1_u21C5_ 64, if a v1_u2250_ 67; a f15 b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as G4, apply f15 to a and b, then mirror it around E4; otherwise compute a f15 b.

operators.name: f24
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C3, move a up one step of C major, then lower it an octave; otherwise move a up one step of C major.

operators.name: f25
operators.plain: If a is the same note as G4, apply f16 to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] and (a f6); otherwise apply f6 to a.

operators.name: f26
operators.plain: If a equals [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2], apply f4 to a and b, then mirror it around D4; otherwise compute a f4 b.

operators.name: f27
operators.definition: a f27 b = { (a v1_u27F7_ b) - 3, if a v1_u2250_ 62; a v1_u27F7_ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as D4, measure the semitones from a to b, then subtract 3 from it; otherwise measure the semitones from a to b.

operators.name: f28
operators.plain: If a equals [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2], apply f22 to a and b, then apply f4 to the result and [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2]; otherwise compute a f22 b.

operators.name: f29
operators.plain: If a equals [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2], mirror a around b, then apply f18 to the result and [D4:1 F4:2]; otherwise mirror a around b.

operators.name: f30

operators.name: f31

operators.name: f32
operators.definition: a f32 b = { - (a v1_u27F7_ b), if a v1_u2250_ 67; a v1_u27F7_ b, else }

operators.name: f34

operators.definition: a f35 b = { 2 - (a v1_u27F7_ b), if a v1_u2250_ 67; a v1_u27F7_ b, else }
